The assumptions in the provided text regarding turkey cooking time are consistent with standard mathematical and physical modeling principles for heat transfer. Assuming constant oven temperature simplifies the boundary conditions of the differential equation governing heat conduction. Assuming uniform density allows for the use of simplified thermal diffusivity models, although real turkeys have varying densities due to bone, skin, and fat, this is a common and acceptable approximation for estimation problems. The assumption of full defrosting is also physically sound, as starting with a frozen turkey would require significant additional energy for phase change (latent heat of fusion), drastically altering the time-temperature profile.
